title: Radio call — positive identification
plain: Open the exchange with the railway initials and engine number digit by digit, then say who you are. Both parties identify before anything moves.

title: Radio call — clear, sighted, and the movement
plain: Confirm you are in the clear with a visual on the tail car, then give the movement with a direction and a distance. Direction is taken off the front of the locomotive.

title: Radio call — a distance every call
plain: The running count carries a distance every call, said twice, tagged with the engine number. The engineer repeats each count back.

title: Radio call — point protection on the count
plain: You keep the tail car and the joint in sight the whole way in. The calls tighten as the gap closes.

title: Radio call — inside two car lengths
plain: At or below two car lengths the engine number comes off and the call stays short. The engineer still repeats it back.

title: Radio call — the last car count
plain: The final car-length count before the switch to feet. Real, correct practice — no CROR paragraph is cited for it in the verified source, so it is played and explained but never graded.

title: Radio call — distance counts take over
plain: Past the last car you count distance, not cars. A car length is fifty feet, so a half car is about twenty-five.

title: Radio call — twenty feet
plain: Closing distance in feet, short and steady so the engineer can ease it in. No CROR paragraph is cited for the closing counts in the verified source — played and explained, never graded.

title: Radio call — ten feet
plain: Closing. No CROR paragraph is cited for the closing counts in the verified source — played and explained, never graded.

title: Radio call — five feet
plain: The last call before the stop. No CROR paragraph is cited for the closing counts in the verified source — played and explained, never graded.

title: Radio call — stop and stretch the joint
plain: One call brings the brakes on to stop, then asks the engineer to pull against the coupling to prove it is a proper joint. Watch it — the cars must not pull apart.

title: Radio call — set and center
plain: Three-step protection before anyone goes between equipment. This is CN practice (a General Operating Instruction), not a CROR rule — so it is never graded. The nearest CROR precaution is Rule 109.

title: Radio call — hoses coupled, air cut in
plain: Under set-and-center protection you couple the air hoses, open the angle cocks, and report it back. Going-between protection and cutting the air in are CN practice, not CROR-worded — never graded.

title: Radio call — air to the tail
plain: The engineer confirms the air has charged through to the tail; you repeat it back and tell him you are going for the hand brakes. Hand brakes are not released until the air is sufficiently charged.
